basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 34.' and it opens '| Vers. 34. Viri pastores sumus, et patres nostri. Haec est justa servitus, ut homines'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 34. Viri pastores sumus, et patres nostri. Haec est justa servitus, ut homines pecoribus dominentur, et pecora hominibus serviant. Nam humanam servitutem aut iniquitas aut adversitas facit. Iniquitas quidem, sicut Noe maledicens filio suo dixit: Maledictus filius meus Chanaan, servus erit fratribus suis. Adversitas, sicut Joseph, qui venditus factus est servus. Detestantur Aegyptii omnes pastores ovium. Jure Aegyptus mundum istum significat, in quo abundavit iniquitas. Abominantur Aegyptii pastores ovium, quia omnis iniquus odio habet justum. In terra Gessen. Gessen dicit esse Thebaidem regionem, quae a LXX Gosen vocatur.
